Consult Summary:
- 53-year-old male with 1-week history of atraumatic left elbow swelling and warmth, clinically assessed via video as likely olecranon bursitis; started on OTC ibuprofen and arranged for blood tests (inflammatory/infectious/rheumatologic/gout screen) with safety-netting and follow-up plan.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Left elbow swelling noticed ~1 week ago in shower; feels like fluid-filled; slightly warm.
- Symptom characteristics:
  - Pain: Denies pain at rest; mild tenderness adjacent to swelling on palpation.
  - Function: Full range of motion; able to move elbow normally.
  - Local signs: Slight warmth; patient notes “feels a bit strange.” Doctor observed dry skin on tip of elbow.
  - No known trauma or overuse; sedentary desk job.
  - No prior episodes.
  - Reports it “feels a bit better now.”
- Exacerbating/relieving factors: Not specified.
- Associated symptoms/ROS mentioned: Denies eczema; no other systemic symptoms discussed.
- Family history queried for rheumatologic disease (RA/lupus): Patient initially unsure, later denied.

Past Medical History:
- Osteoarthritis: Previously diagnosed by GP “a few years ago.” No associated current treatment mentioned.
- Allergies:
  - Peanuts.
  - No known medication allergies.
- Medications: None regularly.

Social History:
- Occupation: Desk job; not physically strenuous.
- Physical activity: Runs 2–3 times per week.
- Tobacco/alcohol/substance use: Not documented.

Family History:
- No known family history of rheumatoid arthritis or lupus (patient initially unsure, then denied; conflict noted).

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Not documented.
- Musculoskeletal (video exam, left elbow):
  - Visible swelling at elbow.
  - Slightly warmer than surrounding skin (per patient).
  - Mild tenderness adjacent to swelling on palpation (per patient).
  - Dry skin at tip of elbow (observed by clinician).
  - Full range of motion (per patient).
- No additional findings documented.

Investigations:
- Planned:
  - Blood tests: Inflammatory markers, infection screen, rheumatologic antibodies, and gout screen.
  - Logistics: Forms to be mailed; instructions provided; expected results in ~5–6 days after testing.
- Results: None yet.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Left elbow swelling, likely olecranon bursitis (atraumatic; warm; fluid-like; preserved ROM; improving; no current concern for septic arthritis on video assessment)
  - Start OTC ibuprofen 400 mg twice daily after food; stop if heartburn occurs.
  - Blood tests as above to evaluate inflammatory/infectious/rheumatologic and gout etiologies.
  - Follow-up after blood tests to review results and reassess joint; option for in-person or virtual visit per patient preference.
  - Safety-net: Seek urgent care if elbow becomes very red, very painful, or if redness spreads/worsens (concern for septic arthritis).
- Issue 2: History of osteoarthritis (previous GP diagnosis)
  - No acute intervention today; monitor.
- Issue 3: Peanut allergy
  - Noted; no acute issues discussed.

General plan items:
- Reassurance provided that current presentation is not life-threatening and does not appear to be septic arthritis.
- Patient advised to contact clinic sooner if deterioration occurs.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: Vitals; comprehensive ROS (fever, chills, systemic symptoms not documented); full medication reconciliation (OTC/herbals not documented); smoking/alcohol history; immunization status; detailed musculoskeletal exam maneuvers beyond ROM; imaging not discussed; no aspiration considered/discussed in transcript.
- Internal conflicts: Family history—patient initially unsure, later denied rheumatologic conditions (conflict noted).
- Transcript quality: Generally clear; minor filler/overlap; adequate for clinical documentation.
